invariants: all public stateful operations use inherent instance methods
request and response framing follow RFC 9112 message body length precedence
transfer-coding lists accept optional whitespace around commas without including it in coding tokens
response field list tokens are parsed in place with optional whitespace case folding and malformed empty elements rejected
Transfer-Encoding together with Content-Length is rejected as conflicting framing
duplicate Content-Length fields are rejected by the strict security policy
a request with a non-final chunked transfer coding is rejected as indeterminate
HEAD informational 204 and 304 responses have no message body
successful CONNECT responses expose a tunnel instead of an HTTP body decoder
an unframed response is close-delimited while an unframed request has no body
encoded decoded chunk-line trailer-byte and trailer-field limits are independently bounded
chunk data terminators and trailer field syntax are validated incrementally
the caller owns decoded output and the decoder does not retain complete encoded input
BodyProgress consumed bytes stop before pipelined input after body completion
range bounds are validated before decoder or caller-owned output mutation
range decoding reports consumed bytes relative to the requested range without an intermediate input copy
completion validates terminal framing without consuming the decoder so an aggregate owner can perform one typestate move
finish consumes the decoder and rejects incomplete fixed-length or chunked bodies
